channel.description: Recent content in Freedom on Pivtorak.Studio

item.title: 001 Iran – Persia: A Civilizational Transition
item.description: The first civilizational case study of The Asterisk Problem, combining Ethical Resonance and Systemic Solution Manifesto across thirty interconnected works.

item.title: 005 The Right to Learn to Fly
item.description: Young birds learn to fly through practice, uncertainty, and courage. This article explores the universal right to learn, fail safely, and discover one’s own wings.

item.title: 006 Independent Researcher Manifesto: The Right to Human Outcomes
item.description: Systems, models, and institutions are instruments of navigation. Their value is determined by whether they help people live, love, create, return home, and build the future.

item.title: 08-02 Point of Transition. Refusal of the "Republic"
item.description: After establishing continuity and legitimacy, Persia rejects the false label of ‘Republic’ that concealed authoritarian rule. This work explores the restoration of semantic honesty, where the name of the state must correspond to its true essence: freedom.

item.title: 08-03 Point of Transition. The True Name: Persia
item.description: After dismantling false labels, Persia restores its historical name. This work explores naming as a mechanism of state identity, reconnecting civilizational memory with future democratic statehood.

item.title: 09-01 Persia 2.0: Global Dimension. Freedom as Structure (Open Ecosystem)
item.description: Persia proposes a new global model in which freedom functions as infrastructure. Open protocols, transparent institutions, and visible systemic flows create stability through openness rather than force.

item.title: ✯ Extra Credit Problem (The Asterisk Problem)
item.description: A multidisciplinary research framework examining countries and regions where freedom, human dignity, child protection, and individual agency face systemic challenges. Each case study maps the path from tragedy and diagnosis to recovery, subjectivity, and civilizational renewal.

item.title: Freedom and Meta-Control
item.description:
Freedom and Meta-Control#

In the world of modern management, it is commonly believed that success is derived from rigid planning, minute-by-minute control, and endless to-do lists. But for a person with autonomous thinking and a high level of internal responsibility, such an approach often becomes a “cognitive prison.”
